newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki spurred by Nokia, but correction in view.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki spurred by Nokia, but correction in view.

text.p: Shares closed a lively session up for the fourth day in a row on Tuesday, as Nokia rallied after gains on Wall Street. But brokers said a correction was in sight.
The HEX rose 0.18 percent to 2,156.63, its highest close since October 2, 1995. Volume was a healthy 412 million markka, with Nokia accounting for slightly more than half of the total.
Brokers said the recent strong gains could give way to a downward correction.
"I think shares will correct lower on Wednesday as we have risen quite a lot during the last few days," one broker said.
Nokia closed active trade 1.00 markka up at 197.50 after breaking 200.00 markka for the first time since end-May. One broker saw the share's resistance level at about 210.00 markka.
Markka strength and recent bearish views by sector analysts sent forestries slightly lower, brokers said. Enso shed 0.40 markka to close at 37.30, but UPM-Kymmene ended flat at 99.50.
Software house TT Tieto was lifted by positive analyst comments, brokers said. The share closed up 5.00 markka at 245.00 after hitting a new life-high 250.00 in fair trade.

Metals and mining group Outokumpu advanced one markka in lively trade helped by recent gains in cyclical stocks on Wall Street. Steel group Rautaruukki closed unchanged at 40.00 markka after hitting a calendar year-high 40.50 in fair trade.
